newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids mixed.

text.p: Spring wheat cash bids were mixed on Thursday with a bias to the upside in sympathy with higher MGE futures, dealers said.
Dealers cited a pickup of movement and concerns about potential flooding this spring in the northern Midwest spring wheat growing region, which could delay plantings.
"It is a little warmer here and some snow is starting to melt," a Minneapolis dealer said.
Usually, spring wheat planting in Minnesota and North Dakota begins in April, depending upon weather. "But we will not determine if we are late until we get into May," he said.
In North Dakota, some Red River Valley producers who are in low-lying areas continued to move grain to local elevators.

The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration issued a warning this week that spring flooding could be more widespread this year than in any year in the past decade -- especially in the upper Midwest.
One Montana dealer added movement was brisk in high protein hard red winter wheat. "It was very good," the dealer said.
MGE May spring wheat futures gained 4-1/4 cents to end at $4.11-1/2 a bushel with the rest of the board nine to 16 cents up.
